summary:
The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 authorizes appropriations and sets policies for the Department of Defense (DOD), Department of Energy national security programs, the Department of State, and the Intelligence Community. The Act is organized into seven divisions. Below are the primary purposes and major provisions across all parts of the bill.

The Act authorizes specific funding levels for military activities. It sets Operation and Maintenance funding at approximately $288.8 billion, Military Personnel funding at $176.8 billion, and various other authorizations, including $38.3 billion for the Defense Health Program. It authorizes $645.9 million for the Intelligence Community Management Account, $514 million for the CIA Retirement and Disability Fund, and $198.5 million for the Merchant Marine Academy.

Regarding military personnel, compensation, and benefits, the bill authorizes a 5.2 percent increase in basic pay for service members. It expands Basic Needs Allowance eligibility to service members in areas with a "demonstrated need" beyond just a high cost of living. For the Blended Retirement System, continuation pay eligibility is lowered from 8 years of service to 7. A monthly bonus is authorized for service members below the grade of E-6 beginning January 1, 2024, due to prevailing economic conditions, and ending December 31, 2024. Various expiring bonus and special pay authorities are extended through December 2024. The bill also creates permanent parental leave pay for certain reserve component members, effective October 1, 2024. The military requires that accessions and promotions be based solely on individual merit and demonstrated performance. Additionally, the bill halts the creation or filling of new diversity, equity, and inclusion positions at DOD until a specific Government Accountability Office review is complete.

For force structure and major weapons systems, the Act places several restrictions on retiring or reducing legacy aircraft fleets. The Air Force is prohibited from using funds to retire or reduce the inventory of A-10, KC-135, F-15E, F-16C/D, T-1A, E-3 AWACS, and RQ-4 aircraft, subject to specific numerical floors, annual reporting, and sunset dates. For instance, the limitation on F-15E retirements lasts until October 1, 2029, and RQ-4 restrictions apply until September 30, 2028. The Navy is required to maintain a minimum of nine carrier air wings. The bill authorizes multiyear procurement for up to 13 Virginia class submarines. It also establishes the Space Force Personnel Management Act as a standalone title in U.S. code, creating a new, independent personnel management system.

In acquisition policy and management, the "Never Contract with the Enemy" program is renamed "Threat Mitigation in Commercial Support to Operations," its authorities are overhauled, and its sunset is extended to December 31, 2033. The temporary authority for the DOD to modify contracts due to inflation is extended through December 31, 2024. Beginning October 1, 2027, the DOD is prohibited from procuring batteries produced by several named Chinese companies, including CATL and BYD.

On foreign and intelligence matters, the bill authorizes the Secretary of Defense to expend up to $40 million per fiscal year for clandestine activities to support foreign forces and establish non-conventional assisted recovery capabilities. The State Department is required to review all special envoy positions to determine which are necessary. For country reports on human rights, the bill mandates a new description of transnational repression acts. The Intelligence Community must develop a plan to recruit, train, and retain personnel with financial intelligence and emerging technology expertise. The Director of National Intelligence must issue a community-wide policy on prepublication review within 30 days. The climate security advisory council’s sunset is moved up to December 31, 2024.

The bill also contains other miscellaneous but significant provisions. It designates March 9 as "U.S. Hostage and Wrongful Detainee Day" and mandates a new flag be flown at certain government buildings. It makes it a federal crime for a foreign official to demand a bribe from a U.S. person. The JROTC program is expanded to a target of 3,400 to 4,000 units, with increased and restructured instructor compensation. Finally, it prohibits DOD funds from being used to endorse critical race theory.
